blocks.text: 扩展智能体预测环境

inlines.text: 扩展智能体预测环境

blocks.text: 预测分为两个阶段：研究与预测。在上一篇文章中，我们介绍了如何训练模型，在其他智能体完成研究的基础上做出预测。本文则对 Inkling 2 Small 做后训练，让它在单次智能体 rollout 中同时完成这两步。每个环境都会给智能体一道预测题，以及用于时点研究、执行代码和提交概率分布的工具。

blocks.text: 要开展这项工作，我们需要：(1) 比公开平台所能提供的更多高质量题目；(2) 快到足以支撑数千个并发 rollout 的研究工具。

blocks.text: 大规模、高质量的题目生成

inlines.text: 大规模、高质量的题目生成

blocks.text: 公开可用的高质量预测题很有限。2026 年在 Metaculus、Polymarket 和 Kalshi 上结算的数值题约有 84.8 万道，去重后剩约 30.4 万道，剔除偏题（体育、天气和加密货币价格）后剩约 6600 道，再剔除低质量题目（某人会说什么、视频播放量、次日价格）后只剩约 3900 道。

blocks.text: 为了解决数据不足的问题，我们构建了一套系统，用 LLM 直接从新闻中生成合成预测问题，思路类似于 Bosse et al. (2026) 和 Turtel et al. (2026)。我们借助这套系统生成了 45,000 道问题，组成训练题库。我们重点关注定量问题，例如“截至 2026 年 6 月 30 日，日本外务省最近一次报告显示波斯湾还剩多少艘船只？”这些生成的问题与真实分布足够接近，因此模型的表现能够泛化到预测网站上的留出问题（图 4）。

inlines.text: 低延迟、高带宽的时点工具

blocks.text: 智能体的研究工具返回的是时点数据，也就是在提问当时可以获取、而非之后才出现的信息（例如新闻、维基百科、经济时间序列）。

blocks.text: 训练期间，我们在数千个并发环境中生成 rollout。在这种规模下，直接调用第三方数据 API 会让训练慢到无法进行。受各接口速率限制的影响，本文描述的这次训练如果按那种方式跑，大约需要九年才能完成。

blocks.text: 于是我们改为持续从这些 API 摄取数据，存入自建数据库，以低延迟访问（图 5）。例如，我们维护了一份维基百科完整修订历史的专用时点副本：1.32 TB 的索引和嵌入文本。公开的维基百科 API 只能搜索今天的维基百科，而且获取历史版本时每次请求只能返回一个页面；我们的智能体则可以对任意历史日期的维基百科做语义搜索，并在一次查询中读取整批历史页面。

blocks.text: 预测是一个带噪声的优化问题

inlines.text: 预测是一个带噪声的优化问题

blocks.text: 在对现实世界事件做概率预测时，奖励是随机的。就任何单道问题而言，一个过度自信的预测可能胜过一个符合真实潜在分布的预测（示例见图 6）。

inlines.text: 在对现实世界事件做概率预测时，奖励是随机的。就任何单道问题而言，一个过度自信的预测可能胜过一个符合真实潜在分布的预测（示例见图 6）。

blocks.text: 过度自信的预测往往得分更高。结果从可能结果的分布 P* 中逐个抽取，每个结果都用对数分数分别评估两个预测：校准预测 p₁（等于 P*）和过度自信预测 p₂。每个结果随后按得分更高的一方着色，加入下方的堆叠。在 250 个模拟世界中，p₂ 有 60% 的情况得分更高，但 p₁ 平均领先 1.16 nats。

blocks.text: 为了应对这种随机性，我们把结果对数分数与一个期望对数分数混合，后者基于一个强参考预测——用同一道问题在我们的 harness 上运行前沿模型集成得到。

blocks.text: 参考预测被用作近似最优预测，其依据是受训模型可获得的信息。用该参考下的期望对数得分作为奖励，可以降低单个问题结果带来的随机性，并且只反映智能体本可知道的信息。代价是会偏向于前沿模型的错误。混入结果对数得分能让奖励锚定在真实结果上，同时保留大部分随机性的降低。

blocks.text: 智能预测能力在训练中涌现

inlines.text: 智能预测能力在训练中涌现

blocks.text: 我们在 Tinker 上分多个阶段、以不同的推理强度进行后训练。我们用 StableReinforce 做异步在途采样的强化学习——这是 Tinker 的一种方法，能让强化学习在长时间运行中保持稳定。我们基于 Inkling 2 Small 构建，因为它的基础能力使其接近预测帕累托前沿，对微调响应良好，而且通过 Tinker 提供服务时训练器与采样器之间的不匹配程度很低。我们刻意让测试框架保持轻量、不做硬性规定，这样智能体能自己学习策略，而不是遵循硬编码的策略。

blocks.text: 在低强度下，微调后的智能体通过更高效地找到关键信息，以更低的成本超越了 Inkling 2 Small Base 的预测。在高强度下，智能体更像一名量化分析师：它会穷尽式地研究，并编写代码分析数据，然后再构建最终分布（图 8）。

blocks.text: 后训练模型进行了更高效、更深入的分析。在训练问题上，每次预测的成本和推理 token 数相对于 Inkling 2 Small Base（强度 0.9）的比值，运行 20 次或更多搜索的预测占比，以及在 Python 沙箱中运行代码两次或更多次的预测占比。

blocks.text: 具体来看一个问题：韩国银行公布的2026年8月煤炭和石油产品生产者价格指数会是多少？基础版 Inkling 2 Small 进行了25次工具调用和4次代码调用。它阅读了新闻，在指数与以韩元计价的油价之间拟合了一条直线，并得出结论：该指数下降的速度几乎与油价一样快，提交的中位数为225。经过微调的 Inkling 2 Small 进行了49次工具调用和9次代码调用。它发现炼油厂价格上限已被冻结，燃油税减免持续到7月底，然后逐月对照迪拜原油对指数建模，发现油价每变动1%，当月只有约0.38%传导到该指数。它用2022年油价暴跌来检验这一点——当时该指数下跌21%，而油价下跌31%——并提交了一个中位数为272的分布，预计将缓慢下降。

blocks.text: 结论与后续步骤

inlines.text: 结论与后续步骤

blocks.text: 我们后训练版本的 Inkling 2 Small 拓展了预测的成本-准确率前沿，在每次预测成本低15倍的同时，达到了 Fable 5.2（中等）的水平。取得这一结果意味着要解决端到端训练智能体预测器带来的三个问题。第一，公开问题稀缺，所以我们自己生成问题，并验证在这些问题上的改进能泛化到真实问题。第二，实时研究 API 对大规模强化学习来说太慢，所以我们从自己的数据库提供时点数据。第三，预测奖励噪声很大，所以我们构建了一个包含参考预测的新奖励函数。

blocks.text: Scaling agentic forecasting environments

inlines.text: Scaling agentic forecasting environments

blocks.text: Forecasting involves two stages: research and prediction. In our previous post, we described training a model to make predictions given research done by other agents. Here, we post-train Inkling 2 Small to do both in a single agentic rollout. Each environment provides the agent with a forecasting question and tools to run point-in-time research, execute code, and submit a probability distribution.

blocks.text: To unlock this work, we needed: (1) a much larger supply of high-quality questions than public platforms offer, and (2) research tools fast enough to serve thousands of concurrent rollouts.

blocks.text: Large-scale, high-quality question generation

inlines.text: Large-scale, high-quality question generation

blocks.text: Publicly available, high-quality forecasting questions are limited. Of ~848k numerical questions resolved on Metaculus, Polymarket and Kalshi in 2026, ~304k remain after removing duplicates, ~6.6k after removing off-topic questions (sports, weather and crypto prices), and ~3.9k after removing low-quality questions (what someone will say, video views, next-day prices).

blocks.text: We started with popular prediction markets, but after deduplicating across platforms and filtering out off-topic and immaterial questions, a small fraction remained usable for training.

blocks.text: To address the shortfall, we built a system that generates synthetic forecasting questions directly from the news with LLMs, analogous to Bosse et al. (2026) and Turtel et al. (2026). We used this system to produce a pool of 45,000 questions for use in training. We focused on quantitative questions, such as “How many vessels will Japan’s Foreign Ministry have most recently reported as remaining in the Persian Gulf by 30 June 2026?” These generated questions are sufficiently on-distribution that performance generalizes to the held-out questions from prediction sites (Figure 4).

blocks.text: Instead, we ingest data from these APIs continuously and store it in our own databases that we can access at low latency (Figure 5). For instance, we maintain a dedicated point-in-time copy of Wikipedia’s complete revision history: 1.32 TB of indexed and embedded text. The public Wikipedia API can only search today’s Wikipedia, and returns historical versions one page per request; our agent can run semantic searches over Wikipedia as it was on any past date, and read a whole batch of historical pages in a single query.

blocks.text: Forecasting is a noisy optimization problem

inlines.text: Forecasting is a noisy optimization problem

blocks.text: In probabilistic forecasting about real-world events, the rewards are stochastic. On any single question, an over-confident forecast can outperform a forecast that matches the true underlying distribution (see Figure 6 for an example).

blocks.text: An overconfident forecast often scores higher. Outcomes are drawn one at a time from P*, the distribution of possible outcomes, and each is scored with the log score against a calibrated forecast p₁ (equal to P*) and an overconfident forecast p₂. Every outcome then joins the pile below in the color of whichever forecast scored higher. Across 250 simulated worlds, p₂ scores higher 60% of the time, yet p₁ is ahead by 1.16 nats on average.

blocks.text: The reference forecast is used as an approximation to the optimal forecast given the information available to the model being trained. Using the expected log score under this reference as the reward reduces the stochasticity of a single question’s resolution and reflects only what the agent could have known. The tradeoff is a bias toward the frontier models’ errors. Mixing in the outcome log score keeps the reward anchored to real outcomes while preserving most of the reduction in stochasticity.

blocks.text: Intelligent forecasting capabilities emerge through training

inlines.text: Intelligent forecasting capabilities emerge through training

blocks.text: We post-train on Tinker in several stages, at different reasoning efforts. We do asynchronous in-flight sampling for RL with StableReinforce — a Tinker method that keeps RL stable across long runs. We build on Inkling 2 Small because its base capabilities place it close to the forecasting Pareto frontier, it responds well to fine-tuning, and trainer/sampler mismatch is low when served through Tinker. We keep the harness deliberately lightweight and non-prescriptive, so the agent learns its own strategies rather than following hardcoded ones.

blocks.text: Concretely, take one question: what would the Bank of Korea report as the August 2026 producer price index for coal and petroleum products? Base Inkling 2 Small made 25 tool calls and four code calls. It read the news, fit one straight line between the index and the oil price in won, and concluded the index would fall almost as fast as oil, submitting a median of 225. The fine-tuned Inkling 2 Small made 49 tool calls and nine code calls. It found that refinery price caps had been frozen and a fuel-tax cut ran to the end of July, then modeled the index month by month against Dubai crude and found that only about 0.38% of each 1% oil move reaches the index in the same month. It tested this against the 2022 oil crash, when the index fell 21% while oil fell 31%, and submitted a distribution with a median of 272, expecting a slow decline.

blocks.text: Conclusion and next steps

inlines.text: Conclusion and next steps

blocks.text: Our post-trained version of Inkling 2 Small extends the cost-accuracy frontier for forecasting, matching Fable 5.2 (medium) while being 15× cheaper per forecast. Achieving this result meant solving three problems that come with training an agentic forecaster end-to-end. First, public questions are scarce, so we generate our own, and test that improvements on these generalize to real questions. Second, live research APIs are too slow for RL at scale, so we serve point-in-time data from our own databases. And third, forecasting rewards are noisy, so we built a new reward function that includes a reference forecast.

Achieving this result meant solving three problems that come with training an agentic forecaster end-to-end. First, public questions are scarce, so we generate our own, and test that improvements on these generalize to real questions. Second, live research APIs are too slow for RL at scale, so we serve point-in-time data from our own databases. And third, forecasting rewards are noisy, so we built a new reward function that includes a reference forecast.

blocks.text: Looking ahead, we’re improving and scaling up our post-training stack: expanded forecasting-specific mid-training, novel approaches to long-horizon credit assignment, bigger datasets with sensible curricula, and scaled post-training compute. Our ambition is that every high-stakes decision, across the economy, will be better informed by large-scale AI forecasting.
